newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases as market slows down.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases as market slows down.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index easing marginally on Tuesday, bourse officials said.
The index lost 3.41 points to close at 3347.45. Turnover was posted at 19.5 million shillings on 340,000 shares compared to 19.8 million shillings on 539,000 shares on Monday.
"Today was extremely dull for a Tuesday," one broker said.
Despite making gains for three successive trading sessions, a majority of brokers maintained that these were temporary and part driven by selected index-linked shares trading erratically.
"The market is low, and should remain in a lull at least for the short term," a senior broker said.
Brokers observed that especially local investors who favoured short-term gains appeared to be at cross-roads over their next investment move.
"Many of them have started looking ahead at the coming elections," another broker said.
Kenya will hold general elections sometime this year.
The broker added that with a very high degree of risk-averseness among local investors, they were unlikely to lock their money in equities.
Foreign investors traded Kenya Commercial Bank at between 95 and 96 from 95 and Uchumi Supermarket at 37.25 and 38 from 36.50.
Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 9 from 8.90 while Sasini Tea & Coffee rose to 76.50 from 76.
Barclays Bank gained a shilling to 100 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 44.75 from 44.50.
Kenya Airways was unchanged at 8.20 while Nation Printers & Publishers eased to 116 from 117.
The Central Bank of Kenya floating rate treasury bond traded 250,000 shillings at 100.6667 percent compared to 100.5545 percent on Monday.
